patch_description: Instead of greedy construction + 2-opt swaps, I use simulated annealing over full permutations with mixed move operators (adjacent swaps, block reversals, and reinsertion moves). Reinsertion moves are far more effective than pure swaps for sequencing problems because they can move a conflicting transaction across many positions at once. The annealing starts from the best of a few greedy constructions (warm start) and uses a geometric cooling schedule with restart-to-best on improvement, giving a fundamentally different search paradigm: stochastic hill-climbing over the whole solution space rather than deterministic local descent, which escapes local minima that trap the current 2-opt approach.
